text:
maria: Quick heads-up — opening a small TF refactor PR to dedupe provider blocks and flatten the network/module dependency graph. Link: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/4123
raj: Nice. Does this change provider versions anywhere? we have a few stacks pinned to 3.x that could break.
maria: Good call. I left provider versions untouched where modules explicitly depend on 3.x. For the hoisted provider block I pinned to ~> 4.24 (we already use 4.* in most places). Diff snippet: 
```hcl
provider "aws" {
  region  = var.region
  version = "~> 4.24"
}
```
emma: Will CI regenerate the lockfile automatically or do we commit an updated lockfile?
maria: I updated the PR to include a lockfile update for the root module. CI runs `terraform init -upgrade` in a disposable workspace and posts a plan artifact. Ops-bot should show results.
taylor: Any risk of duplicate provider entries in downstream module lockfiles? might need a quick script to consolidate.
maria: Yes, duplicates can happen. I added a tiny script: `scripts/tf-lock-dedupe.sh` that runs `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64` in each module and then we run a compare to decide which lockfile to keep.
raj: Can you paste the script snippet here?
maria: ```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
for d in modules/*; do
  pushd "$d" >/dev/null
  terraform init -backend=false -input=false
  terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64 || true
  popd >/dev/null
done
```
sasha: I skimmed the PR — looks good. One request: add a migration note in the CHANGELOG explaining manual steps for any orgs that fork old modules.
maria: will do. Also ping @raj @emma for a quick LGTM when you have a sec. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: CI: terraform-lockfile-update — plan succeeded (see artifacts) https://ci.redwood/job/4123/plan
raj: LGTM pending the CHANGELOG line and CI artifact check.
emma: LGTM from me as well, thanks for the script.
